alex (DevEx): FYI customers reporting failures after we rearranged package layout. Simple Next edge sample dies on import. Repro: clone samples/next-edge, yarn, hit /api/generate -> 500 with a parse error.

ben (SDK): Which release? We tweaked exports map in 1.2.1 to remove main and be export-conditional only.

alex (DevEx): Exactly. Our package.json now looks like: 
```\n{\n  \"name\": \"@redwood/sdk\",\n  \"version\": \"1.2.1\",\n  \"type\": \"module\",\n  \"exports\": {\n    \".\": { \"import\": \"./dist/esm/index.js\", \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/index.js\" },\n    \"./client\": { \"import\": \"./dist/esm/client.js\", \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/client.js\" }\n  }\n}\n```

alex (DevEx): Error is a SyntaxError on import: unexpected 'export' from the edge runtime stack. Also editors lose intellisense because types not visible.

sam (eng-runtime): Sounds like bundler/resolver ambiguity: some environments (vercel/edge) will prefer require conditions unless exported entrypoints prioritize import. With type: "module" + require subpath, node resolution can get confused when bundling.

katie (TS): For editor/TS issues: tsc and many IDEs look for a top-level "types" or "typings" entry. Subpath-only types inside exports won't be picked up by older tooling. We need to ship a root-level types field pointing to dist/types/index.d.ts.

ben (SDK): Agreed. I think we should do three things: 1) add root "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts", 2) add an explicit `"./edge"` export that is ESM-only to be imported by edge runtimes, 3) reorder the default export to prefer import over require for ambiguous bundlers.

jeff (support): We already patched a customer's monorepo by adding an alias in their next.config.js to force the esm build. That's fragile. They'll want an official fix.

alex (DevEx): Example proposed exports change: 
```\n{\n  \"exports\": {\n    \".\": { \"import\": \"./dist/esm/index.js\", \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/index.js\", \"types\": \"./dist/types/index.d.ts\" },\n    \"./edge\": { \"import\": \"./dist/esm/edge.js\" },\n    \"./package.json\": \"./package.json\"\n  }\n}\n```

katie (TS): Add `typesVersions` if we need to remap subpaths for older tsserver versions. Also make sure `package.json` export exists so some bundlers can read the package manifest.

sam (eng-runtime): We'll add a small runtime test in CI that runs the Next edge sample with `NODE_OPTIONS=--conditions=import` and verifies the edge route returns 200. That should catch regressions.

ben (SDK): I'll open a patch release PR with the changes, include a tiny sample update and CI job, and a migration note in samples/README.

ci-bot: CI started for branch fix/exports-edge-1970001111 :hammer_and_wrench:

ben (SDK): PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1271. It contains: root types, ./edge export, ./package.json subpath, and CI test.

ajex (DevEx): (typo) alex meant to say thanks 😅

jeff (support): Once PR merges, I'll reach out to the affected customers and recommend a temporary pin to 1.2.0 if they can't accept patches immediately.

katie (TS): Also add a line in the DX docs about `@redwood/sdk/edge` for edge-only contexts until old bundlers catch up.

sam (eng-runtime): Recommendation: avoid `type: "module"` at package root unless every subpath is ESM-first; it's a common source of subtle resolver differences.

alex (DevEx): Good plan. Will monitor the CI and update the customers thread. Cheers. :thumbsup:
